text.1: He had ten seconds to escape the dungeon, and he spent four of them looting.
text.2: The ceiling is crumbling. The exit is forty steps away.
text.3: He grabs one chest. Overencumbered. His speed drops to almost nothing.
text.4: So he swaps it for a smaller chest. Still too heavy.
text.5: Wait. Why doesn't he just drop everything and run?
text.6: You see, losing something hurts twice as much as gaining it feels good. Scientists call it loss aversion.
text.7: So he drops his loot one item at a time. Every drop costs him a second.
text.8: Finally, he lets go of everything and sprints.
text.9: The floor collapses behind every step.
text.10: The door is locked. The key was in the first chest.
text.11: He kicks it open with one second left.
text.12: He escapes with zero gold, zero swords, and one apple.
text.13: It was the only thing the game let him carry.
